issues.title: feat(cli): decide and implement query exit codes for empty results
issues.description: `sep47idx query` exits 0 when nothing matches. Issue #17 asked for exit code 2; CLAUDE.md §5.12 reserves 2 for "not found". Decide whether an empty filter result is "not found" and implement it consistently for text, JSON and CSV.
issues.why: Scripts that ask "is anything implementing SEP-41?" need to tell an empty answer from success without parsing output.
acceptance_criteria: The decision and its reason are recorded in docs/cli.md.

Tests cover an empty result in each output mode.

issues.title: feat(sepmeta): decode contract event specs and expose Events()
issues.description: `pkg/sepmeta` turns `contractspecv0` function entries into `FnSig` values, but event entries (`SC_SPEC_ENTRY_EVENT_V0`) are decoded and then ignored. Add an `Events(spec)` function that returns each event's name, prefix topics, parameters (name, type, location: topic or data) and data format, using the same canonical type names as `Functions`.
issues.why: SEP-41 defines `mint` and `clawback` as events, not functions. Without event specs the inferred tier can only ever check half of the token interface.
acceptance_criteria: `Events` returns every event entry in spec order, with types rendered exactly like `Functions` (`Address`, `Option<T>`, `udt:Name`, ...).
The token fixtures' events (`transfer`, `approve`, `burn`, `mint`, `clawback`, where present) are asserted in table tests.
Malformed or truncated event entries become errors, never panics; `FuzzDecodeSpec` covers the new code path.
`doc.go` and `docs/how-it-works.md` describe what is and is not read from event specs.
guidance: Start from `TypeName` in `pkg/sepmeta/spec.go`; reuse it rather than writing a second renderer.
go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0 changed `ScSpecEventV0.Name` to a `string` (see its CHANGELOG); handle the new type.

issues.title: feat(sepmeta): resolve user-defined types into a type table
issues.description: Functions that take structs, unions, enums or error enums render today as `udt:Name` with no structure. Build a `Types(spec)` table that decodes every UDT entry (fields, cases, values) and lets callers resolve a `udt:` reference to its definition, including nested and forward references.
issues.why: Rule files for SEP-40 (`Asset`, `PriceData`) and SEP-56 need to compare type structure, not only names. The type table is the foundation for that.
acceptance_criteria: Struct fields, union cases (void and tuple), enum and error-enum values are decoded with their types.
References to undefined types and reference cycles are reported as errors with the type name, never followed forever.
Table tests cover each UDT kind using the existing fixtures plus a new hand-built spec stream.
Every length read from the spec is bounded by `Limits` before allocation.
guidance: UDT names were widened to 1024 bytes in go-stellar-sdk v0.8.0; respect `Limits` for them.
Keep the API read-only and allocation-bounded like the rest of the package.

issues.title: feat(sepmeta): decode contractenvmetav0 and record each Wasm's interface version
issues.description: Soroban Wasm carries a `contractenvmetav0` custom section with the environment interface version the contract was built against. Decode it in `pkg/sepmeta`, store it with each analysed Wasm, and expose it in `sep47idx wasm` and `/v1/wasm/{hash}`.
issues.why: The interface version shows which protocol a contract targets. It lets the adoption report say whether declarations correlate with newer toolchains, and flags code built for an older protocol.
acceptance_criteria: `ReadCustomSections` callers can request the section; a decoder returns the protocol and pre-release fields with bounds checks.
A migration adds a nullable column (operator approval for the schema change is recorded in the PR before coding).
Fixtures assert the decoded value; Wasm without the section stores NULL, not 0.
API and CLI output include the field without changing existing response fields.
guidance: CLAUDE.md requires operator approval for schema changes after the first migration; open the design in the issue first.
Mirror how `has_meta`/`has_spec` are written in `internal/ingest/analyze.go`.

issues.title: feat(sepmeta): read custom sections from an io.ReaderAt with bounded memory
issues.description: `ReadCustomSections` takes the whole module as a `[]byte`. Add a variant that walks sections from an `io.ReaderAt` (with a known size), reading only section headers and the requested custom sections, so large modules never need to be fully resident.
issues.why: The indexer receives code from RPC as a single blob today, but offline inspection of local Wasm files and future data-lake backfills read from files. Peak memory should scale with the requested sections, not the module.
acceptance_criteria: The new function returns byte-identical results to `ReadCustomSections` on every fixture and on every fuzz corpus entry (differential test).
All existing limits apply, including the section-count cap, and a short read is `ErrTruncated`.
A benchmark shows peak allocation on a 1 MiB module stays within a stated bound.
`FuzzReadCustomSections` exercises both implementations against each other.
guidance: Keep the byte-slice API as the reference implementation and test the new one against it.

issues.title: test(sepmeta): cross-implementation conformance suite against stellar-cli and py-stellar-sdk
issues.description: Build a recorded conformance suite: for every golden fixture, store the meta and interface output of `stellar contract info` and of the Python stellar-sdk `ContractMeta.supported_seps()`, then assert `pkg/sepmeta` agrees with both (or documents each intentional difference).
issues.why: SEP-47 parsing has three widely used implementations. Recording where they agree, and where soroindex deliberately differs (lenient anomalies), turns parser behaviour into checked evidence.
acceptance_criteria: A script regenerates the recorded outputs with pinned tool versions, recorded in `testdata/contracts/README.md`.
A Go test compares sepmeta's SEP list and anomalies for every fixture and vector with the recorded outputs.
Every difference is listed in a table in `docs/how-it-works.md` with the reason.
Normal `go test` never needs Python or stellar-cli installed.
guidance: Commit the recorded outputs as JSON under `testdata/`, like the existing vectors.
Pin `stellar-cli` and `stellar-sdk` exactly; the e2e note in this repo's history shows why.

issues.title: test(sepmeta): structure-aware fuzzing for SCMetaEntry and ScSpecEntry streams
issues.description: The fuzz targets mutate raw bytes, so most inputs fail XDR decoding in the first few bytes. Add generators that build valid `SCMetaEntry` and `ScSpecEntry` streams from fuzzer-provided choices (counts, nesting depth, string lengths), then feed the encoded bytes to the decoders.
issues.why: Byte-level mutation rarely reaches deep decoder paths such as nested `Map<K, Vec<Option<udt>>>`. Structure-aware inputs reach them in seconds.
acceptance_criteria: New fuzz targets build valid streams and assert decode, re-encode and `Functions` round-trip invariants.
Depth and size are bounded by `Limits`; inputs past a limit must produce `ErrLimit`, never a panic or OOM.
Each target ran for at least 10 minutes locally; the summary is pasted in the PR.
Any crash found is committed under `testdata/fuzz/` with its fix.
guidance: `go test -fuzz` only accepts primitive arguments; derive structure from a `[]byte` seed with a small deterministic decoder.

issues.title: perf(sepmeta): benchmark suite with allocation budgets enforced in CI
issues.description: Add benchmarks for `ReadCustomSections`, `DecodeMeta`, `DecodeSpec`, `ParseSEP47` and `Functions` over the golden fixtures, and a CI check that fails when allocations per operation exceed a committed budget.
issues.why: The parser runs on every Wasm the network deploys. Regressions in allocations would show up as slower seeding long before anyone noticed in review.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmarks report ns/op, B/op and allocs/op for each function and fixture.
Budgets live in a committed file; CI compares `-benchmem` results and fails with a clear message when exceeded.
Numbers measured on the CI runner, with date and Go version, are recorded in `docs/`.
The check runs in under two minutes and is not a required check until the budgets are stable.
guidance: Use `testing.B.ReportAllocs`; avoid timing assertions, which are noisy on shared runners.

issues.title: test(fixtures): add a SEP-40 oracle consumer fixture contract
issues.description: Add a Rust fixture under `testdata/contracts/` that implements the SEP-40 oracle interface exactly as the current SEP text defines it (including its user-defined types), declares `contractmeta!(key="sep", val="40")`, and is built by `scripts/build-fixtures.sh` into a committed golden `.wasm`.
issues.why: The SEP-40 rule file (Soroban-CII/soroindex#20) needs a known-good contract to prove a match, and the parser has no fixture with oracle-style UDTs.
acceptance_criteria: The contract's functions and types are copied from the SEP-40 text at a cited commit.
`scripts/build-fixtures.sh` builds it reproducibly with the pinned toolchain; the Wasm is committed.
sepmeta tests assert its declared SEPs and its `Functions` output.
`testdata/contracts/README.md` records the exact versions used.
guidance: Follow the structure of `testdata/contracts/token_full_sep/`.

issues.title: test(fixtures): add a SEP-50 non-fungible token fixture contract
issues.description: Add a Rust fixture implementing the SEP-50 non-fungible token interface from the current SEP text, declaring `sep=50`, built into a committed golden Wasm.
issues.why: The SEP-50 rule file (Soroban-CII/soroindex#21) needs a matching fixture, and NFTs are the next most common interface question after tokens.
acceptance_criteria: Functions and types follow the SEP-50 text at a cited commit, including any optional functions marked as such.
Built by `scripts/build-fixtures.sh` with the pinned toolchain; the Wasm is committed.
sepmeta tests assert declared SEPs and `Functions` output.
A second variant omits one required function, for partial-match tests.
guidance: Reuse `testdata/contracts/common/` helpers where they fit.

issues.title: test(fixtures): add a SEP-56 tokenized vault fixture contract
issues.description: Add a Rust fixture implementing the SEP-56 tokenized vault interface from the current SEP text, declaring `sep=56` (and `41` if the vault share token is SEP-41), built into a committed golden Wasm.
issues.why: The SEP-56 rule file (Soroban-CII/soroindex#22) needs a matching fixture, and vaults are the first interface that composes with SEP-41.
acceptance_criteria: All vault functions (deposit, mint, withdraw, redeem and their preview/max pairs, per the SEP text) are implemented with the specified types.
Built reproducibly; the Wasm is committed.
sepmeta tests assert declared SEPs and `Functions` output.
The README records how the share-token functions relate to SEP-41.
guidance: Cite the SEP-56 commit you read in the fixture's source comment.

issues.title: test(fixtures): add negative token fixtures for matcher edge cases
issues.description: Add fixture contracts that look like tokens but are not quite: wrong output type on `balance`, `transfer` with swapped argument order, a duplicated function name across modules, and renamed parameters with correct types.
issues.why: The matcher compares types and order, never names. Today only `token_partial` and `not_token` exercise failure paths, so several documented rules have no real-Wasm evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Each fixture is built by the fixtures script and committed.
Matcher tests assert the exact status, `missing` and `mismatched` evidence for each.
Renamed parameters with correct types still produce `match`, proving names are ignored.
The fixture table in `testdata/contracts/README.md` lists each fixture's purpose.
guidance: Keep each fixture minimal: only the functions needed to show the case.

issues.title: ci(fixtures): verify golden Wasm reproduce from their Rust sources
issues.description: Add an optional CI workflow that installs the pinned Rust toolchain and stellar-cli, rebuilds every fixture with `scripts/build-fixtures.sh`, and fails if any rebuilt `.wasm` differs from the committed file.
issues.why: Normal builds never need Rust because the Wasm is committed. Without a reproduction check, a committed fixture can drift from its source and nobody would notice.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow runs on changes under `testdata/contracts/` and on manual dispatch, not on every PR.
Tool versions come from `testdata/contracts/rust-toolchain.toml` and the README, never `latest`.
A mismatch prints the fixture name and both SHA-256 hashes.
Actions are pinned to commit SHAs like `ci.yml`.
guidance: `truncated.wasm` is derived by script from `token_full_sep.wasm`; regenerate it the same way.

issues.title: feat(rules): match event specs in rule files, starting with SEP-41
issues.description: Extend `rules/schema.json` with an optional `events` section (name, topics, data types), teach the matcher to compare them against decoded event specs, and add SEP-41's events to `rules/sep-0041.json` from the current SEP text.
issues.why: SEP-41 specifies events (transfer, approve, burn, mint, clawback) as part of the interface. Checking only functions overstates conformance for contracts that emit nothing.
acceptance_criteria: The schema, matcher and rule file change together; `make rules-check` validates every rule file.
Event results are reported separately from function results, so existing `status` semantics do not silently change.
Golden fixtures prove a match, a missing event and a mismatched event.
A new `ruleset_version` triggers `sync --recompute`; the PR includes its output on a fixture index.
guidance: Depends on event decoding in `pkg/sepmeta` (see the `Events()` issue).
Changing what `match` means is a trust-tier question; get operator agreement on the reporting design first.

issues.title: feat(match): structural matching for user-defined types
issues.description: Let rule files describe a UDT by structure (struct fields with types, union cases) instead of only by name, and make the matcher resolve `udt:Name` through the spec's type table before comparing.
issues.why: Two contracts can define the same `PriceData` struct under different names, or different structs under the same name. Name-only comparison gives wrong answers both ways for SEP-40 and SEP-56.
acceptance_criteria: Rule files can declare a type once and reference it from several functions.
Matching compares field order and types, never field names, consistent with how function parameters are matched.
Tests cover same-structure/different-name (match) and same-name/different-structure (mismatch).
Evidence in `mismatched` shows the expected and found structure.
guidance: Depends on the UDT type-table issue in `pkg/sepmeta`.

issues.title: feat(match): composite rules — a SEP-56 vault requires a SEP-41 share interface
issues.description: Add a `requires` field to rule files so one SEP's match can depend on another's (SEP-56 vault shares are SEP-41 tokens). The matcher evaluates dependencies and reports a composite result with both parts' evidence.
issues.why: Reporting a vault as `match` when its share token interface is broken would overstate trust, which CLAUDE.md's tie-break rule forbids.
acceptance_criteria: `requires` is validated by the schema and cycles are rejected at load time.
A composite result is `match` only when the SEP and every required SEP match; evidence names which part failed.
API and CLI output show the dependency without changing the existing response shape for SEPs without `requires`.
Tests use the SEP-56 and token fixtures.
guidance: Coordinate with the SEP-56 rule file issue (Soroban-CII/soroindex#22).

issues.title: test(match): property and fuzz tests for the matcher
issues.description: Add a fuzz target and property tests for `Match`: results must be deterministic, independent of the order functions appear in the spec, monotonic (adding an unrelated function never lowers a status), and never panic on any `FnSig` input.
issues.why: The matcher decides the inferred tier for every Wasm. Its invariants are documented but only tested with hand-picked examples.
acceptance_criteria: `FuzzMatch` runs against the shipped rule files with arbitrary function lists.
Property tests assert order independence and monotonicity over generated inputs.
`partial_threshold` boundaries (exactly half) are covered.
Ran 10 minutes locally with the summary in the PR; any crash is committed with its fix.
guidance: Generate `FnSig` values from the type names `TypeName` can produce.

issues.title: feat(rules): draft a rule file from a SEP's Rust trait definition
issues.description: Write a small tool (`go run ./scripts/rulegen`) that reads the Rust trait block from a SEP markdown file and emits a draft rule file with functions, input types and outputs, for a human to review.
issues.why: Rule files are written by hand from SEP text today. A generator removes transcription errors and makes reviewing a new SEP a diff instead of a rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: The tool handles the trait syntax used by SEP-41, SEP-40, SEP-50 and SEP-56, and reports anything it cannot parse instead of guessing.
Running it on SEP-41's text reproduces `rules/sep-0041.json`'s functions exactly (a golden test with the markdown committed under `testdata/`).
Output always needs human review: it sets `ruleset_version` to a placeholder that `make rules-check` rejects.
Documented in `docs/rule-files.md`.
guidance: Map Rust types (`Address`, `MuxedAddress`, `i128`, `u32`, `String`) to the canonical names in `pkg/sepmeta/spec.go`.

issues.title: feat(store): record each rule file's SHA-256 with every interface match
issues.description: Store the SHA-256 of the exact rule file used for each `interface_matches` row and expose it next to `ruleset_version` in the API and CLI.
issues.why: `ruleset_version` is a human label. A hash proves which bytes produced a verdict, so a changed file with an unchanged label cannot go unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: A migration adds the column; the schema change has operator approval recorded before coding.
`--recompute` treats a hash change as stale even if the version label is unchanged.
Rows written before the migration show the hash as unknown, never as a guessed value.
Tests cover recompute on hash change and the API field.
guidance: CLAUDE.md fixes the schema after the first migration without operator approval; propose first.

issues.title: feat(match): report extra functions and interface coverage per Wasm
issues.description: Extend `MatchResult` with the functions present in the spec but not in the rule file, and a coverage summary (required OK, optional OK, extra), and show it in `sep47idx wasm` and `/v1/wasm/{hash}`.
issues.why: Contract authors and integrators want to know whether a token is a plain SEP-41 token or a token plus admin functions. Today that information is discarded.
acceptance_criteria: `extra` lists function names in spec order; it never affects `status`.
Stored with the match (schema change approved first) or recomputed from `functions_json`, with the choice explained in the PR.
API output adds fields without changing existing ones.
Tests use the token and not_token fixtures.
guidance: `wasm.functions_json` already stores every function signature.

issues.title: feat(rules): keep historical SEP-41 rulesets and report which version a Wasm matches
issues.description: Ship rule files for earlier SEP-41 versions (before `MuxedAddress` was added to `transfer`) alongside the current one, and report the newest version each Wasm matches.
issues.why: Many deployed tokens predate SEP-41 v0.4.0. Saying which version they implement is more useful, and more accurate, than a single accepted-types list.
acceptance_criteria: Each historical rule file cites the SEP-41 commit it was read from.
The matcher reports the highest matching version; current behaviour for the latest version is unchanged.
`token_full_legacy.wasm` reports the pre-MuxedAddress version; `token_full_sep.wasm` the current one.
API and docs explain the field.
guidance: Read the SEP-41 history in stellar-protocol to find the exact commits.

issues.title: feat(sync): detect a testnet reset and refuse to continue
issues.description: Testnet is periodically reset, which restarts ledger numbers under the same passphrase. Detect it (stored `last_ledger` far ahead of the RPC's latest, or a stored ledger hash that no longer matches) and stop with a dedicated sentinel error and a message telling the operator to start a new index.
issues.why: After a reset, the existing index describes contracts that no longer exist. Continuing would silently mix two networks' histories in one database.
acceptance_criteria: A new sentinel (for example `ErrNetworkReset`) is returned before anything is written.
Detection stores a ledger hash checkpoint in `sync_state` so it does not rely on ledger numbers alone.
Tests simulate a reset with the fake RPC used in `internal/sync/loop_test.go` and assert the database is unchanged.
`docs/how-it-works.md` and the troubleshooting docs explain what to do.
guidance: Today `loop.go` returns a generic error when the stored ledger exceeds the RPC latest; build on that path.

issues.title: feat(sync): record ledger protocol versions and fail clearly on unknown XDR
issues.description: Record the ledger protocol version seen in each batch in `sync_state`, log protocol changes, and when ledger metadata cannot be decoded because of an unknown XDR arm, stop with an error that names the protocol, the ledger and the SDK version to upgrade.
issues.why: Testnet's Protocol 30 upgrade stopped sync with a raw decoder message (`'3' is not a valid StellarValueType`) and took a week to diagnose. The next upgrade should explain itself.
acceptance_criteria: The protocol version is read from each ledger header and stored with the last ledger.
An unknown-XDR failure is wrapped in a sentinel error with ledger, protocol and pinned SDK version in the message.
A test feeds a header with a future `StellarValueType` and asserts the message, using the re-encoding approach in `internal/ingest/protocol30_test.go`.
`stats` and `/v1/health` report the last seen protocol without changing existing fields' meaning.
guidance: The Protocol 30 test shows how to build headers the decoder rejects.

issues.title: feat(ingest): fetch Wasm in parallel with a bounded worker pool and ordered commits
issues.description: New code hashes are fetched and analysed one batch at a time. Fetch and analyse them with a bounded pool (using `--rpc-concurrency`), while keeping commits in ledger order and the one-transaction-per-batch rule.
issues.why: Seeding mainnet took 18 minutes on a resumed run. Most of that is waiting on RPC round trips that could overlap.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrency is bounded by the configured value; no unbounded goroutines.
Results are committed in deterministic order, and replaying a batch is still idempotent (the replay test passes unchanged).
Cancellation stops all workers and leaves `last_ledger` at the previous batch.
A benchmark with a fake RPC that adds latency shows the speed-up; numbers are recorded with the machine and date.
guidance: `internal/rpc` already retries with backoff; do not add a second retry layer.

issues.title: feat(ingest): verify fetched code against its ledger key hash
issues.description: When contract code is fetched with `getLedgerEntries`, check that the SHA-256 of the returned Wasm bytes equals the hash in the `ContractCode` key before parsing or storing anything. A mismatch is recorded as a parse error and never produces claims.
issues.why: The index trusts the RPC provider's bytes. A misbehaving or compromised provider could attach another contract's metadata to a hash, and nothing would notice.
acceptance_criteria: Every fetched code entry is hashed and compared before analysis.
A mismatch stores `parse_status='error'` with a clear message and no claims or matches.
Tests use a fake RPC that returns the wrong bytes for a key.
`docs/how-it-works.md` documents the check.
guidance: `internal/ingest/fetch.go` decodes the returned entries; add the check there.

issues.title: test(sync): property-based replay over random fact sequences
issues.description: Generate random but valid sequences of contract facts (creates, upgrades, CAP-85 reference updates, archival and restoration), apply them in different batch splits and with replays, and assert the final database dump is identical every time.
issues.why: The seven §5.9 tests cover chosen scenarios. Idempotency and batch-independence should hold for every sequence, and random sequences find the cases nobody thought to write.
acceptance_criteria: A generator produces valid fact sequences from a seed; failing seeds are printed for reproduction.
The same sequence applied as one batch, many batches, and with a full replay gives identical dumps (reuse the dump helper in `internal/sync/loop_test.go`).
Runs a bounded number of cases in normal `go test` and more under a flag.
Any bug found is fixed in the same PR with a regression test.
guidance: `TestRetentionGapLeavesEveryTableUnchanged` already has a whole-database dump helper.

issues.title: test(store): fault-injection harness that fails every write point
issues.description: Build a test harness that makes the N-th store write fail (for every N in a batch), then reruns sync and asserts the final database equals a clean run.
issues.why: The crash-mid-batch test cancels at one point. A harness that fails at every write proves the one-transaction-per-batch guarantee everywhere, including fetch and analysis writes.
acceptance_criteria: The harness wraps the store's write path without changing production behaviour.
For a recorded batch, every failure point leaves `last_ledger` unchanged and a rerun produces the clean-run dump.
Runs in under a minute in normal `go test`.
Documented in the test file so new write paths are covered automatically.
guidance: `store.Tx` centralises writes through `exec`; inject failures there in tests.

issues.title: ci(sync): nightly read-only mainnet follow job
issues.description: Add a scheduled workflow, like the testnet integration job, that follows mainnet for 30 minutes from the tip against a configured RPC URL (stored as a repository variable or secret), with no transactions and no stored data.
issues.why: Testnet's protocol upgrade broke sync for a week before anyone saw it; mainnet will upgrade too. A nightly mainnet run catches the same failure before users do.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow reads the RPC URL from configuration and skips cleanly, with a notice, when none is set.
It reuses the testnet integration test with the network as a parameter, not a copy.
Pass criteria match the testnet job: no errors over 30 minutes and lag under 10 ledgers at the end.
Not a required check for pull requests; actions pinned to SHAs.
guidance: See `.github/workflows/integration.yml` and `internal/sync/integration_test.go`.

issues.title: feat(config): futurenet network support
issues.description: Add `futurenet` as a third network: passphrase, default RPC URL, database default, docs and tests, everywhere `mainnet` and `testnet` are handled today.
issues.why: Futurenet runs upcoming protocol versions first. Indexing it gives early warning of XDR and contract changes before they reach testnet and mainnet.
acceptance_criteria: `--network futurenet` works for every command; the passphrase is checked against `getNetwork` like the others.
The verify and testnet-only guards keep treating futurenet as not-testnet unless the code is explicitly reviewed.
Config tests cover the new network; docs list it.
The passphrase and default URL are copied from current Stellar documentation, cited in the PR.
guidance: `internal/config/config.go` defines `Network` values.

issues.title: perf(sync): throughput benchmark on a recorded ledger corpus
issues.description: Add a benchmark that replays a committed corpus of real ledgers through `LedgerSource`, change extraction and the store, and reports ledgers per second and allocations; record results in `docs/`.
issues.why: There is no measured number for how fast the indexer applies ledgers, so nobody can tell whether a change made sync slower or whether one machine can keep up with mainnet.
acceptance_criteria: Uses only committed fixtures; no network.
Reports ledgers/s, facts/s and allocations; results with machine, date and Go version are in `docs/`.
Profiles the top three hotspots and lists them in the PR, without necessarily fixing them.
Runs under `go test -bench`, not in normal tests.
guidance: Depends on, or can include, the recorded ledger corpus issue.

issues.title: test(ingest): record a corpus of real testnet ledgers covering every change type
issues.description: Record real `getLedgers` responses that include a Wasm deploy, an instance upgrade, a SAC creation, a CAP-85 executable reference create and update, an archival and a restoration, and commit them with tests asserting the extracted facts.
issues.why: Change extraction is tested on two recorded ledgers plus synthetic XDR. Real ledgers for every change type would catch encoding details synthetic tests miss.
acceptance_criteria: A script finds and records each ledger, writing the RPC response and the source ledger number.
Tests assert the exact facts extracted from each recorded ledger.
Files are trimmed to the needed ledgers and stay small.
`internal/rpc/testdata/README.md` documents how each was found.
guidance: Existing recorded data lives in `internal/rpc/testdata/getLedgers.json`.

issues.title: test(ingest): fuzz change extraction over mutated LedgerCloseMeta
issues.description: Add a fuzz target that mutates recorded `LedgerCloseMeta` XDR and runs decoding plus `ExtractContractFacts`, asserting no panic, bounded memory, and that every successfully decoded ledger yields facts consistent with its own changes.
issues.why: Ledger metadata comes from the network and is untrusted input, but only the Wasm parser is fuzzed today.
acceptance_criteria: Seeds come from the recorded ledgers.
Inputs above the configured XDR limits must fail with a limit error, not allocate.
Ran 10 minutes locally with the summary in the PR; crashes committed with fixes.
Added to `fuzz-smoke` with a short duration.
guidance: `UnmarshalBase64` in `internal/ingest/instance.go` applies the XDR limits.

issues.title: feat(ingest): retry queue for Wasm whose fetch failed
issues.description: When fetching a new code hash fails after the RPC client's retries, record it in a retry queue instead of failing the whole batch, keep sync moving, and retry queued hashes on later batches with backoff.
issues.why: One unreachable entry should not stall indexing of the whole network, but it also must not be silently skipped.
acceptance_criteria: Queued hashes are visible in `stats` and `/v1/stats` as a count.
A queued Wasm has `parse_status` that says so and no claims until it is fetched.
Retries are bounded and logged with the hash only.
Schema changes have operator approval first; tests cover queueing, retry success and permanent failure.
guidance: Claims and matches must never be invented for a Wasm that was not fetched.

issues.title: feat(sync): optional cross-provider ledger-hash verification
issues.description: Add an opt-in mode where each batch's ledger hashes are confirmed against a second RPC provider before commit, and sync stops if the providers disagree.
issues.why: The index trusts one provider for everything. Operators who publish results may want independent confirmation of what they ingest.
acceptance_criteria: Enabled by a flag naming a second RPC URL; both are checked to be on the configured network.
A disagreement stops sync with both hashes in the error and writes nothing.
Tests use two fake RPCs, one returning a different hash.
The cost (extra requests) is documented.
guidance: Ledger hashes are available from the ledger header in `LedgerCloseMeta`.

issues.title: feat(sync): --stop-ledger for bounded, reproducible replays
issues.description: Add `sync --stop-ledger N` to stop after committing ledger N, so an index can be built to an exact ledger for reproducible reports, tests and comparisons.
issues.why: Reports cite ledger numbers, but there is no way to build an index that stops exactly at one. Comparisons between machines or versions need the same end point.
acceptance_criteria: Sync commits through N and exits 0, never past it, even mid-batch (the last batch is shortened).
Combines correctly with `--seed` and `--start-ledger`; invalid ranges exit 1 before any network call.
Tests cover stopping inside a batch and at a batch boundary.
Documented in `docs/cli.md`.
guidance: `ingest.LedgerSource.Fetch` takes a start ledger; add an upper bound.

issues.title: feat(store): track live_until_ledger and expose entries close to archival
issues.description: Store the `liveUntilLedgerSeq` of code and instance entries when they are read, and expose contracts whose code or instance will be archived within a given number of ledgers.
issues.why: Archived code keeps its last known claims, but integrators also want to know which contracts are about to become unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: TTLs are recorded from `getLedgerEntries` responses and from ledger TTL changes, with the source noted.
An API and CLI view lists entries expiring before a ledger; new API parameters get operator approval first.
Unknown TTLs are NULL, never guessed.
Tests cover TTL extension and expiry.
guidance: `rpc.LedgerEntry.LiveUntilLedgerSeq` is already decoded.

issues.title: feat(ingest): record transaction provenance for creations and upgrades
issues.description: Record the transaction hash (and, where the metadata exposes it, the source account) that created each contract and caused each upgrade, and show it in contract history.
issues.why: History shows that a contract changed at a ledger, not which transaction changed it. Auditors want to jump straight to the transaction.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance is read from transaction metadata during change extraction, never inferred.
Schema change approved before coding; missing provenance (seeded rows) is NULL.
History in the API and CLI includes the field.
Tests use recorded ledgers with a known upgrade transaction.
guidance: Changes are already walked per transaction in `internal/ingest/changes.go`.

issues.title: feat(rpc): authenticated RPC providers without logging secrets
issues.description: Support RPC providers that require an API key: read a header name and value from the environment (for example `SEP47IDX_RPC_HEADER`), send it on every request, and guarantee it never appears in logs, errors or stored state.
issues.why: Paid and rate-limited RPC providers need authentication. Without first-class support, operators put keys in URLs, which then appear in logs.
acceptance_criteria: The header is applied by the RPC client; URLs containing credentials are rejected with advice to use the header.
Errors and logs are tested to never contain the header value.
Documented in `docs/self-hosting.md` with the env var name.
No secret is ever written to `sync_state` (`rpc_url` is stored without credentials).
guidance: `internal/rpc/client.go` builds every request in one place.

issues.title: feat(cli): migration status and dry run with checksums
issues.description: Add `sep47idx migrate --status` and `--dry-run`, which list applied and pending migrations, and store a checksum of each applied migration so an edited migration file is detected at startup.
issues.why: Migrations are applied automatically on start. Operators cannot see what will change before it does, and an edited migration would go unnoticed.
acceptance_criteria: `--status` and `--dry-run` make no changes; output lists versions, names and checksums.
Startup refuses to run when an applied migration's checksum differs, with a clear message.
Existing databases without checksums are upgraded once, recording current checksums.
Tests cover pending, applied and tampered migrations.
guidance: Migrations are embedded from `migrations/` via `migrations/embed.go`.

issues.title: test(store): upgrade-path harness across every historical migration
issues.description: Build databases at each historical schema version (from the committed migrations), populate them with representative rows, migrate forward, and assert data and invariants survive.
issues.why: Each migration is tested from empty. Real users upgrade databases full of data, which is where migrations fail.
acceptance_criteria: For every migration N, a database at N-1 with sample rows upgrades cleanly.
All SQL invariants still hold after upgrade (reuse the raw-SQL invariant checks).
New migrations are covered automatically.
Runs in normal `go test` in under 30 seconds.
guidance: `0002_functions_json.sql` is the first real upgrade case: rows before it must show NULL `functions_json`.

issues.title: test(store): query-plan regression tests for every API query
issues.description: For each query behind the API and CLI, assert with `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` that it uses the intended index and never scans `wasm_claims` or `contract_versions` in full.
issues.why: The 1M-row benchmark passed because of indexes. A refactor that drops an index use would only show up as slow production queries.
acceptance_criteria: One test per query lists the expected index names.
Failures print the actual plan.
Covers catalog filters for every tier, contract detail, history, wasm detail, seps, stats and gap.
Documented next to `docs/query-benchmark.md`.
guidance: Plans depend on `ANALYZE`; build the fixture database the same way in every test.

issues.title: perf(store): 10M-claim benchmark and materialization decision record
issues.description: Extend the benchmark to 10 million claim rows and 1 million contracts, measure p50/p95 for every API query, and write a decision record on whether the `claims` view should be materialized at that scale.
issues.why: The 1M benchmark settled the question for today. Adoption growth or factory deployments could reach 10M rows, and the decision should be made from numbers, not guesses.
acceptance_criteria: The fixture builder is reproducible from one command.
Results include machine, date, Go version and database size.
If p95 exceeds 200 ms, the record compares a materialized design with measured before/after numbers.
Results are added to `docs/query-benchmark.md`.
guidance: `internal/store/catalog_benchmark_test.go` builds the current 1M fixture.

issues.title: feat(cli): maintenance command for ANALYZE, vacuum and integrity checks
issues.description: Add `sep47idx maintenance` that runs `PRAGMA integrity_check`, `ANALYZE` and an incremental vacuum safely while no sync is writing, and reports what it did.
issues.why: A long-running index grows and its query statistics go stale. Operators need a supported way to keep it healthy instead of hand-written SQL.
acceptance_criteria: Refuses to run while another process holds the write lock, with a clear message.
Reports integrity results, size before and after, and duration.
Tests run it on a fixture database and on a deliberately corrupted copy.
Documented in `docs/self-hosting.md` and `MAINTAINING.md`.
guidance: modernc.org/sqlite supports these pragmas; keep `CGO_ENABLED=0`.

issues.title: feat(api): serve several networks from one process
issues.description: Let `sep47idx serve` open one read-only database per network (for example `--db mainnet=...,testnet=...`) and route requests by network, with each response's `network` field correct.
issues.why: Public deployments want mainnet and testnet behind one endpoint. Running two processes doubles operations work for no benefit.
acceptance_criteria: The route design (path prefix or query parameter) is approved before coding, since API paths are a fixed surface.
Each store is opened `mode=ro` and checked against its network passphrase.
Single-network flags keep working unchanged.
Handler tests cover both networks and an unknown network.
guidance: CLAUDE.md §5.11 fixes API paths; propose the design in the issue first.

issues.title: feat(store): data-quality checker against the RPC
issues.description: Add a command that samples N stored contracts, reads their instance entries from the RPC, and reports any whose executable (Wasm hash, SAC or CAP-85 reference) differs from the index at the index's `last_ledger`.
issues.why: Sync is tested offline, but nothing checks the live index against the network. A sampled comparison is cheap evidence the index is right.
acceptance_criteria: Sampling is random but reproducible with a seed.
Differences are reported with contract ID, stored value and RPC value; exit code 1 when any differ.
Accounts for contracts changed after `last_ledger` so a lagging index is not reported as wrong.
Tests use a fake RPC; docs describe running it weekly.
guidance: `internal/ingest/seed.go` already reads instance entries by contract ID.

issues.title: feat(store): publish nightly read-only database snapshots
issues.description: Add a workflow and command that build a consistent snapshot of a seeded testnet index, compress it, and publish it with a SHA-256 checksum so users can start from a snapshot instead of seeding.
issues.why: Seeding takes many minutes and an RPC with good limits. A verified snapshot lets anyone query the index in seconds.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshots use a consistent SQLite backup, never a raw copy of a live file.
Each snapshot records network, `last_ledger`, schema version and parser version in a manifest.
Users can start `sync` from a snapshot and continue; tested end to end.
Retention and hosting location are documented; secrets are never in the snapshot.
guidance: Depends on the online backup command (Soroban-CII/soroindex#44).

issues.title: feat(api): ETag and If-None-Match on every GET endpoint
issues.description: Return an `ETag` derived from the response's `as_of_ledger`, parser version and ruleset versions (plus the request's query), and answer `304 Not Modified` to a matching `If-None-Match`.
issues.why: Most API reads repeat between ledgers. Conditional requests let clients and caches skip unchanged responses at no risk of staleness, because the tag changes whenever the index advances.
acceptance_criteria: Every `/v1` GET sets a strong ETag; error responses do not.
`If-None-Match` with a matching tag returns 304 with no body; any change to `last_ledger`, parser or ruleset version changes the tag.
Tests cover each endpoint, a stale tag and a weak/invalid header.
`docs/api.md` documents the behaviour with a real captured request.
guidance: Compute the tag from values already read for the response; do not hash the whole body unless needed.

issues.title: feat(api): request IDs, access logs and a Prometheus-text /metrics endpoint
issues.description: Add middleware that assigns each request an ID (returned in a header), writes one structured `slog` access line per request, and exposes request counts and latency histograms per route at `/metrics` in Prometheus text format, using only the standard library.
issues.why: An operator running the public API has no request logs or latency numbers today, so slow queries and abuse are invisible.
acceptance_criteria: Access logs include route pattern, status, duration and request ID, and never full query strings with cursors or any request body.
`/metrics` is off by default and enabled with a flag; its path choice is approved since API paths are a fixed surface.
Histograms use fixed buckets; output parses as valid Prometheus exposition format (tested).
No new dependency.
guidance: `internal/api/server.go` `ServeHTTP` is the single entry point.

issues.title: test(api): fuzz every query-parameter parser
issues.description: Add fuzz targets that drive each endpoint's parameter parsing (`implements`, `implements_any`, `tier`, `kind`, `limit`, `cursor`, path IDs and hashes) with arbitrary strings through the real handlers on a fixture store.
issues.why: API parameters are untrusted input. Handler tests check chosen bad inputs; fuzzing checks that no input panics, leaks internals or returns a non-standard error shape.
acceptance_criteria: Every response is either 200 with valid JSON or one of the documented error codes in the standard shape.
No response body contains file paths, SQL or Go type names.
Ran 10 minutes per target locally, with summaries in the PR; crashes committed with fixes.
Added to `fuzz-smoke` with a short duration.
guidance: Reuse the fixture store helpers in `internal/api/server_test.go`.

issues.title: feat(api): versioned, tamper-evident cursors with stable ordering during sync
issues.description: Version the cursor format, reject cursors from another schema or ruleset version with a clear 400, and prove that paging through results while sync commits new rows never repeats or skips a row that existed when paging started.
issues.why: Keyset cursors are opaque base64 today. A cursor reused across an upgrade, or paging during sync, can give confusing results with no explanation.
acceptance_criteria: Cursors carry a version; old or foreign cursors return `bad_request` with a message saying to restart paging.
A test pages through `/v1/contracts` while a writer inserts rows and asserts no duplicates or gaps among the original rows.
Tampered cursors are rejected without revealing why beyond `invalid cursor`.
`docs/api.md` documents cursor lifetime.
guidance: `internal/store/pagination.go` encodes cursors.

issues.title: feat(api): archived and executable-reference filters for /v1/contracts
issues.description: Propose and implement filters on `/v1/contracts` for archived state and for contracts that share a CAP-85 executable reference owner, with keyset pagination and the existing tier rules.
issues.why: Integrators ask which tokens are still live, and which contracts upgrade together through one reference. Today they must page everything and filter client-side.
acceptance_criteria: Parameter names and semantics are approved by the operator before coding (fixed API surface).
Filters combine with `implements`, `implements_any`, `tier` and `kind`; SACs never appear under `tier=declared`.
Tests cover each filter alone and combined, pagination, and bad values.
Queries use an index (asserted with a query-plan test).
guidance: `idx_contracts_ref` already indexes reference contracts.

issues.title: feat(api): Server-Sent Events stream of contract upgrades
issues.description: Propose and implement a read-only SSE endpoint that streams new contract versions (contract ID, old and new Wasm hash, ledger, kind) as the index commits them, with resume from a ledger via `Last-Event-ID`.
issues.why: Wallets and monitoring tools want to know when a token they hold is upgraded. Polling history for every contract does not scale.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint path and event shape are approved before coding.
Events come only from committed rows; the API process stays read-only.
Resume from `Last-Event-ID` replays missed versions within a bounded window.
Connection limits and idle timeouts are configurable; tests cover resume and disconnect.
guidance: `contract_versions` holds every version with `from_ledger`.

issues.title: feat(api): HTTP server hardening with timeouts, header limits and slow-client tests
issues.description: Make the server's read-header, read, write and idle timeouts and the maximum header size configurable with safe defaults, and add tests that a slow-loris client and oversized headers are cut off without affecting other clients.
issues.why: The API is meant to be public. Default `net/http` settings let slow clients hold connections open indefinitely.
acceptance_criteria: Defaults are documented and applied in `serve`; flags and env vars override them.
Tests open slow and oversized connections against a real listener and assert they are closed within the limits.
Graceful shutdown still completes in-flight requests.
`docs/self-hosting.md` lists the settings.
guidance: `cmd/sep47idx/cmd_serve.go` constructs the `http.Server`.

issues.title: feat(pkg): typed Go client for the /v1 API
issues.description: Add `pkg/client`: a typed client for every `/v1` endpoint with context timeouts, the standard error shape as a Go error type, and iterators that follow cursors.
issues.why: Go integrators otherwise rewrite the same HTTP and pagination code, and get tier handling wrong. A small official client documents the contract in code.
acceptance_criteria: Every endpoint has a method returning the response types from `internal/store` (or public copies of them).
Iterators follow `next_cursor` until done and stop on context cancellation.
Errors expose the API `code` for `errors.As`.
Tests run against the real handler via `httptest`; package docs include a runnable example.
guidance: Keep it dependency-free, like the rest of the module.

issues.title: test(api): golden response snapshots for every endpoint
issues.description: Build a fixture index from the golden Wasm and recorded ledgers, then snapshot every endpoint's JSON response (with a `-update` flag), so any change in response shape shows up as a reviewable diff.
issues.why: The contract detail shape is a fixed surface (CLAUDE.md §5.11). Field-by-field assertions cover parts of it; a snapshot covers all of it.
acceptance_criteria: Snapshots cover every endpoint, a SAC, a CAP-85 reference contract and an upgraded contract.
Volatile values (timestamps) are normalised, not dropped.
`go test ./internal/api -update` regenerates snapshots; CI fails on drift.
`docs/api.md` examples are checked against the snapshots.
guidance: CLAUDE.md §4: golden files live under `testdata/` with a `-update` flag.

issues.title: feat(api): toolchain statistics endpoint
issues.description: Propose and implement an endpoint that reports the distribution of Rust, SDK and CLI versions found in Wasm meta (`rsver`, `rssdkver`, `cliver`), with declaration and SEP-41 match rates per SDK version.
issues.why: Outreach works best aimed at toolchains: if declarations only appear with recent SDKs, the fix is documentation for that SDK.
acceptance_criteria: Endpoint design approved before coding.
Counts come from stored `meta_json`; unknown or missing versions are their own bucket.
Weighted by unique hash and by contract, like the adoption report.
Tests use fixtures with known meta; documented in `docs/api.md`.
guidance: `wasm.meta_json` keeps all raw meta pairs.

issues.title: feat(api): bulk contract lookup
issues.description: Propose and implement a read-only way to fetch summaries for many contract IDs in one request (for example `GET /v1/contracts?ids=C...,C...`), with a cap on IDs per request.
issues.why: Wallets check every token a user holds. One request per contract is slow for them and wasteful for the server.
acceptance_criteria: Design approved before coding; the response reuses existing summary shapes.
Every ID is validated as a contract strkey before any query; unknown IDs are reported, not dropped silently.
The cap is enforced and documented; rate limiting counts the request fairly.
Tests cover mixed valid, unknown and invalid IDs.
guidance: Contract ID validation already exists in the API package.

issues.title: feat(cli): inspect a local Wasm file without a database
issues.description: Add `sep47idx inspect <file.wasm>` that runs the parser, claim sources and matcher on a local file and prints the declaration, anomalies and interface verdict with the missing/mismatched evidence, with `--json`.
issues.why: Contract authors want to check their build before deploying. Today they must deploy, wait for the index, then look up the hash.
acceptance_criteria: Works offline, needs no database or RPC, and applies the same limits as the indexer.
Output matches what `sep47idx wasm` would show for the same code after indexing (tested with fixtures).
Exit codes: 0 for analysed, 1 for errors, with an optional flag to exit non-zero unless a given SEP matches.
`docs/contract-authors.md` uses it instead of the deploy-then-query flow.
guidance: Reuse `internal/ingest/analyze.go` so results cannot drift from the indexer.

issues.title: feat(cli): doctor command for index and environment checks
issues.description: Add `sep47idx doctor` that checks the database (schema version, network passphrase, integrity quick check), the RPC (reachable, same network, latest ledger), lag, and disk space, and prints a pass/fail line for each.
issues.why: When something goes wrong, operators work through these checks by hand from the troubleshooting notes.
acceptance_criteria: Each check prints a clear result and a fix suggestion; `--json` gives machine-readable output.
Exit code is non-zero if any check fails.
No check writes to the database.
Tests cover each failure with fixtures and a fake RPC.
guidance: `stats --lag` already verifies the RPC network before reading the tip.

issues.title: feat(cli): export the index as a CSV bundle with a manifest
issues.description: Add `sep47idx export --out dir/` that writes contracts, versions, wasm, claims, anomalies and matches as CSV files, plus a manifest with network, `last_ledger`, schema, parser and ruleset versions and a SHA-256 per file.
issues.why: Researchers want the data in their own tools. A documented, checksummed bundle is reproducible evidence; ad-hoc SQL dumps are not.
acceptance_criteria: Exports read one consistent snapshot of the database.
CSV columns are documented and stable; tiers stay in separate columns.
Large tables stream without loading into memory.

issues.title: feat(cli): diff two Wasm hashes
issues.description: Add `sep47idx diff <hashA> <hashB>` that compares two stored Wasm: meta keys, declared SEPs and anomalies, functions added, removed or changed, and the interface verdict for each SEP.

Tests use the token_full_sep and token_partial fixtures.

issues.title: feat(cli): configuration file support for every command
issues.description: Support a JSON config file (`--config` or `SEP47IDX_CONFIG`) for common and command flags, with precedence flags > env > file > defaults, documented and tested.

issues.title: feat(cli): a GitHub Action that checks a contract's declared SEPs
issues.description: Publish a composite GitHub Action in this repository that downloads a pinned `sep47idx` release, runs `sep47idx inspect` on a contract's built Wasm, and fails the job if a required SEP is not declared or not matched.

issues.title: feat(cli): machine-readable errors and a documented error catalog

issues.title: feat(cli): outreach report for undeclared interfaces

issues.title: feat(phase0): toolchain census and declaration rate by SDK version

issues.title: feat(phase0): automate the Hubble census with a cost guard

issues.title: test(sync): 24-hour testnet soak run with lag and memory limits

issues.title: feat(security): configurable Wasm and XDR limits with validated bounds
issues.description: Expose the parser and XDR limits (total Wasm size, per-section size, section count, XDR depth and base64 length) as flags and env vars, validate them against hard upper bounds, and record the limits used in `sync_state`.

issues.title: test(security): bound RPC response sizes and JSON decoding
issues.description: Audit and test how the RPC client handles oversized, deeply nested or slow responses: cap response body size, reject excessive nesting, and time out slow bodies, with tests against a hostile fake server.

guidance: `internal/rpc/client.go` reads every response.

issues.title: docs(security): threat model
issues.description: Write a threat model covering untrusted Wasm and XDR, RPC provider trust, the public read-only API, the release pipeline and the verified tier's subprocess, with each mitigation linked to the code or test that enforces it.
issues.why: The project makes strong safety claims (never executes Wasm, bounds every length). A threat model shows how each claim is enforced and where the gaps are.
acceptance_criteria: Each threat lists impact, mitigation and the enforcing code or test.
Gaps become linked issues rather than prose.
Reviewed against the current code, not the design document.
Added to the docs site and linked from SECURITY.md.
guidance: Start from CLAUDE.md §4 and §5.1 and check each against the code.

issues.title: docs: end-to-end tutorial "find every SEP-41 token"
issues.description: Write a tutorial that goes from nothing to answering "which testnet contracts implement SEP-41?" with the CLI and the API, separating declared, inferred and protocol results, with every command and output captured from a real run.
issues.why: The docs explain each part, but nothing walks a new user through the main question the project exists to answer.
acceptance_criteria: Every command was run; outputs are pasted with the date and ledger.
Explains why the declared, inferred and protocol counts differ, using the trust-tier definitions.

guidance: CLAUDE.md §5.14: every number comes from a real run, with a date.

issues.title: docs: troubleshooting guide for every error
issues.description: Write a troubleshooting page that lists every sentinel error and common failure (retention gap, network mismatch, schema too new, RPC on another network, rate limiting, Protocol upgrade decode errors), each with a real reproduction, its message and the fix.

Linked from error messages where practical.

issues.title: test(e2e): offline end-to-end test of sync, serve and every endpoint

issues.title: docs(rules): calibrate the partial threshold from census data

issues.title: docs: architecture page with diagrams

issues.title: feat(api): configurable CORS allowed origins

issues.title: docs(api): /v1 compatibility and deprecation policy

Linked from `docs/api.md` and the README.

issues.title: feat(api): gzip response compression

issues.title: feat(api): rate-limit response headers

issues.title: docs(self-hosting): systemd units for sync and serve
